tasks.title: Add the audit round reader
tasks.acceptance:
- A reader for recorded audit rounds implements §2.1's five definitions: the trimmed non-empty role predicate (never case-folded, reserved regression id not special-cased), the byte-exact PASS predicate matching the record path, and the four contributes-no-rows causes (empty file entry, unreadable file, a non-blank line that does not unmarshal into a JSON map, an empty or differing stored roles_hash).
- Each no-rows round emits exactly one output.Notice from §2.1's five-row advisory table, chosen by the fixed evaluation order: the hash test first with its empty case before its differing case, then the three file-based causes in table order. engine.LoadRoundRows and its existing callers are unchanged.
- Tests 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 pass, including the discriminating halves: a bare null line is a row, a trailing newline is not a parse failure, and the corpus wording wins over the missing-file wording on a round to which both apply.
tasks.closed_reason:
- internal/engine/auditrounds.go implements §2.1's five definitions: AuditRowRole trims the role string and drops empty/whitespace-only/non-string values without ever case-folding (so "Spec-Coverage" stays a distinct id) and does not special-case the reserved regression id; AuditRowIsPass is byte-for-byte cli.countAuditFindings' status != PASS test; ReadAuditRoundRows implements the four contributes-no-rows causes (empty file entry, unreadable file, a non-blank line that does not unmarshal into a JSON map, an empty or differing stored roles_hash).
- Each no-rows round emits exactly one output.Notice from the five-row advisory table in the fixed evaluation order — empty stored hash, differing stored hash, empty file entry, unreadable file, unparseable line — verified in internal/engine/auditrounds_test.go by asserting captured stderr equals the expected wording exactly (one line, no second advisory), plus a multi-bad-line fixture that still costs one advisory.
- engine.LoadRoundRows and its existing callers are unchanged: no file outside internal/engine/auditrounds.go and its test was touched, and the test asserts LoadRoundRows still reports the same not-found for an empty file entry and for a missing file, which is why §2 needs its own reader.
- Tests 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 11 pass in internal/engine/auditrounds_test.go, including the discriminating halves: a bare null line is a row carrying no role and non-PASS while 5, "x", true and [] each make the round contribute no rows; a trailing newline, a blank line, a whitespace-only line and CRLF endings all contribute rows with no advisory; and the corpus wording wins over the missing-file wording on a round that both differs in hash and has no file on disk. Six mutations (case-fold role, trim status, drop the blank-line skip, require a JSON object, read the file before the hash test, let an empty stored hash match an empty latest hash) each failed a named assertion and were reverted. Gate: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0.

tasks.title: Compute per-role clean streaks
tasks.acceptance:
- role_streaks carries one entry per role in the latest recorded round as {role, consecutive_clean, open}, spec-coverage first and the rest ascending by byte order, and is an emitted empty array — never null, never omitted — whenever no role appears there.
- The walk starts at the latest round and stops when every latest-round role's streak is closed, when a round contributes no rows, or at the start of history, so the §2.1 advisory can fire at most once per invocation.
- Tests 1, 2, 3, 4, 12, 13, 16 and 17 pass, including that a round absent a role ends that role's streak rather than being skipped, and that a corpus change between recorded rounds truncates the streak.

tasks.title: Report spec-coverage streak by name
tasks.acceptance:
- spec_coverage_clean_rounds carries the spec-coverage role's consecutive_clean, or an explicit JSON null when the latest recorded round contributes no row attributed to that id, in §2.1's sense of contributes.
- The key is always emitted, including when its value is null and including under --compact; null and 0 are never collapsed.
- Test 18 passes, with its discriminating half: null when the latest round holds no spec-coverage row even though an earlier round does.

tasks.title: Build the divergence object
tasks.acceptance:
- divergence is emitted only when all five §2.4 conditions hold, and is an omitted key rather than null otherwise; condition 5 is plain equality between the latest round's stored roles_hash and the corpus hash computed now, and constrains --status alone.
- Its five fields are always present when the object is emitted: other_roles_open, open_roles (each id once, ascending, [] when every open row is unattributed), unattributed_open (0 rather than absent), message in one of the three §2.4 forms with the counts taken from spec_coverage_clean_rounds and other_roles_open, and hint equal to the §2.6 constant verbatim.
- Tests 14, 15, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 and 26 pass, including that condition 4 withholds the object at a resolved audit_clean_rounds of 0 and that an unreadable corpus withholds it by both routes.

tasks.title: Emit the signal on both audit outputs
tasks.acceptance:
- spec_coverage_clean_rounds, role_streaks and divergence appear on tp audit <spec> --status with or without --check, and on tp audit <spec> --record <file> computed after the round is stored; they appear nowhere else, including tp audit --merge, tp audit <spec> prompt emission and every tp review mode.
- --compact keeps all three whole, including divergence.message and divergence.hint and the null-valued spec_coverage_clean_rounds key; the audit fields --compact already drops are unchanged.
- Tests 10, 27, 28, 29 and 31 pass, including that --check carries the same payload it carries without the flag.

tasks.title: Guard the untouched convergence gate
tasks.acceptance:
- A guard test asserts that a fixture whose latest round holds only non-spec-coverage findings still reports clean false and converged false, that tp audit --status --check still exits 1, and that next_action is still the fix-and-re-audit directive on the same invocation that emits divergence.
- engine.Converged, engine.ConsecutiveClean, the stored per-round clean flag, AuditNextAction and tp resume are unchanged, and the test fails any implementation that lets the divergence signal reach convergence arithmetic or the next_action precedence.
- Test 30 passes.

tasks.title: Define the mechanized class predicate
tasks.acceptance:
- An entry is valid when engine.ValidateChecks accepts it on its own, judged per entry and never over the slice, so one invalid entry never changes another entry's treatment and a class named by two entries is simply registered.
- A class is mechanized when a valid entry's class equals it byte-for-byte, with no trimming and no case folding; over-specification is exempt from the reviewer exclusion list only, and is mechanized for candidate suppression like any other class.
- Tests 34, 35 and 36 pass, including that a slice-level validation suppresses neither class and fails.
source_sections: ## 3. A registered check retires its mechanize candidate
tasks.closed_reason:
- engine.IsMechanizedClass and engine.ReviewerExclusionClasses in internal/engine/mechanized.go judge validity per entry through the unexported checkIsValid, which calls engine.ValidateChecks on a one-element slice — the same single-entry call runMechanicalChecks makes — so one rejected entry never changes another entry's class and the cross-entry duplicate-class rule is unreachable, leaving a class named by two entries simply registered and named once in the exclusion list.
- The class comparison is plain == against the entry's class: no trimming, no case folding, so a reviewer-written "Duplicate-Line" or " duplicate-line " is not mechanized by a registered duplicate-line entry.
- over-specification is mechanized like any other class in IsMechanizedClass (the candidate-suppression sink) and is dropped from ReviewerExclusionClasses alone, after invalid entries are dropped and before duplicates collapse, so the prompt cannot both demand and forbid the class.
- internal/engine/mechanized_test.go covers the predicate halves of tests 34, 35 and 36 plus the §3.2 filter order and non-nil shape; verified by mutation: whole-slice validation fails the per-entry and two-entry tests, EqualFold+TrimSpace fails the exactness test, exempting over-specification in IsMechanizedClass fails the scoped-exemption test, and collapsing duplicates before dropping invalid entries fails the filter-order test. Gate green: go test ./... exit 0, golangci-lint run exit 0.
Out of scope: the end-to-end halves of tests 34-36 assert mechanize_candidates, mechanized_classes and both prompt-emission sites, which are the sinks owned by candidate-suppression, exclusion-list and mechanized-classes-field; this task ships the predicate they consume.

tasks.title: Suppress mechanized classes from candidates
tasks.acceptance:
- tp review <spec> --record filters mechanize_candidates, the register-a-check hint and the class list handed to next_action; tp review <spec> --status filters the class list handed to next_action through its own separate call over the recorded rounds.
- The frequency threshold is unchanged and suppressing one class never changes whether another crosses it; the filtered mechanize_candidates stays an emitted array and never becomes null.
- Tests 32, 33, 38, 39, 40 and 45 pass, including that tp review --report still lists a registered class and that the varying side of the exactness test is the finding row's class.

tasks.title: Filter the reviewer exclusion list
tasks.acceptance:
- The Mechanically checked classes list takes three membership changes in order — drop invalid entries, drop over-specification, then collapse duplicates keeping the first survivor — and keeps registration order otherwise; when the result is empty the sentence is not appended at all.
- Both assembly sites change: the multi-role panel in internal/cli/review.go and the tp review <spec> --perspective regression path in internal/cli/review_regression.go. The surrounding checks-running branch and the panel path's review_loop instruction addendum keep their own guards.
- Tests 37, 42, 43 and 44 pass, with the all-invalid case asserted through each entry's skipping invalid check notice over a fixture that resolves a task file.

tasks.title: Emit the mechanized classes field
tasks.acceptance:
- mechanized_classes is emitted on tp review <spec> --record and nowhere else, carrying the withheld candidate classes each once and sorted ascending, and survives --compact alongside mechanize_candidates.
- It is always an array on that output — [] when nothing was withheld, never an omitted key and never null — and it never lists a registered class that failed to reach candidate frequency.
- Test 41 passes, with the null half as its discriminating assertion.

tasks.title: Document the release for drivers
tasks.acceptance:
- README.md and skills/tp/SKILL.md each contain the substring `audit convergence still counts every non-PASS row` and the substring `a registered check retires its mechanize candidate`.
- Both describe the three new audit fields and the suppression rule accurately enough for a driver to act on them without reading the spec.

tasks.title: Document the field shapes in REFERENCE
tasks.acceptance:
- skills/tp/REFERENCE.md documents the JSON shape of role_streaks, spec_coverage_clean_rounds, divergence and mechanized_classes.
- It contains all five §4 sentences verbatim, including the divergence.hint constant as sentence 5.

tasks.title: Point the audit-scope rule at the field
tasks.acceptance:
- CLAUDE.md's audit-scope rule contains the substring `tp audit now reports spec_coverage_clean_rounds` and names it as the field carrying the number the rule previously told the driver to track by hand.
- The rest of that rule is unchanged: the audit still runs to two consecutive clean rounds and a spec-scoped finding still blocks the release.

tasks.title: Guard the documentation substrings
tasks.acceptance:
- A guard test asserts README.md and skills/tp/SKILL.md each contain both required substrings, that CLAUDE.md contains `tp audit now reports spec_coverage_clean_rounds`, and that skills/tp/REFERENCE.md contains the five verbatim sentences.
- The REFERENCE.md sentence-5 assertion compares against the same constant the code emits as divergence.hint, so the document and the code cannot drift apart.
- Test 46 passes.
